about.title: Discover the Chronicle
about.description: The Chronicles of Georgia is a monumental work by sculptor Zurab Tsereteli — 16 massive pillars standing 35 meters tall on the shores of the Tbilisi Sea. Construction began in 1985 and remains officially unfinished. The pillars depict biblical and historical scenes from Georgian history.

highlights.h2: Biblical and historical reliefs on each pillar
highlights.h3: Panoramic views of the Tbilisi Sea

items.name: George M.
items.text: Absolutely stunning place! The reliefs on the pillars tell Georgia's entire history. Especially magical at sunset.

items.name: Sarah K.
items.text: A must-see in Tbilisi! The panoramic views are beautiful and the historical pillars are truly impressive.

items.name: David B.
items.text: Tsereteli's masterpiece. A bit far from the center but absolutely worth it. 15 minutes by taxi.

items.name: Maria T.
items.text: Amazing monument! Biblical scenes and Georgian history on the pillars. Perfect for photography.

items.name: Luke J.
items.text: A hidden treasure. Not many tourists, peaceful atmosphere. I recommend visiting in the morning or evening.

items.name: Anna S.
items.text: One of the most impressive monuments I've ever seen. The scale of the pillars is breathtaking.

items.name: Tom W.
items.text: Tbilisi's hidden gem. The view of the Tbilisi Sea from the monument is fantastic.

items.name: Nick P.
items.text: Wonderful spot for photography. Soviet-era monumental art at its finest.

address.label: Address
address.value: QRC6+65V, Chronicles of Georgia Temqa, Tbilisi, Georgia

hours.label: Opening Hours
hours.value: Open 24 hours — Free entry. Best time to visit is sunrise or sunset for photography.

howToGet.label: How to Get There
howToGet.value: From Tbilisi center: 15-20 minutes by taxi. By bus: #60 or #1 towards Tbilisi Sea.

accessibility.label: Accessibility
accessibility.value: Open-air site. Path is partially unpaved — comfortable footwear recommended.
